## My Thinking

I am 55 years old and I have been farming this land since I was a young woman. I never went to school but I have watched this land for thirty years. My mother farmed it before me. I know what this soil wants.

In Quzhou, there is really only one way to farm: winter wheat, then summer corn. That is what every family in my village does. The land rests for nothing — wheat in, corn right after harvest. My 7 mu is flat and the tube well works, so I have no reason to change.

For wheat, I already put down the seeds last October. The variety I bought from the township seed shop — an improved variety the shopkeeper said does well around here. I do not know the name, just the bag. I put down diammonium phosphate before planting and I will spread urea twice more — once when it turns green in spring and once at jointing. I will irrigate four times: the green-up irrigation now that spring is coming, jointing, heading, and grain filling. I spray for aphids in May when everyone else is spraying. I ploughed before planting.

For corn, I plant right after the wheat comes off in June. I buy the hybrid seed — it costs more but I have tried both and the hybrid is clearly better. I know that much without needing to read. I put the fertilizer in the hole with the seed (compound fertilizer) and top-dress with urea at the big bell stage. If July is dry I will water once, maybe twice. I spray for stem borer when I see the village loudspeaker announcement. For corn, I do not plough — I just plant directly into the stubble.

I will not try anything new this year. I am 55, my back hurts, and the market prices for wheat and corn are stable enough. This plan has fed my family for decades.
